clue.text: A nettle cocktail

definitions.meaning: a nettle is a plant that leaves a painful sting on the skin
also the name of a mixed drink of brandy and white crème de menthe

explanation.definitionFit: A nettle hurts whoever brushes it, and the same word names a brandy-and-mint mixed drink.

clue.text: Parties united in Pablo casal's support

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the words Pablo casal's, carried within them

explanation.surface: A musical question about where the cellist Pablo Casals found his backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is padding for the surface: the run sits in paBLO Casal's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of parties or nations acting together.

clue.text: An Asian in alpine resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, so the letters of alpine are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Looking for someone from Asia at a ski resort in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday place, but read it as re-sort: the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nepal, the Himalayan country, is an Asian.

clue.text: Sentimental regard for quiet location

parts.note: soft means quiet, low in volume
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: A fondness for a peaceful place.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a weakness or fond affection for someone is an idiom built on these words.

clue.text: Refusal to admit detective worked miracles

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the letters of miracles are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A sleuth who performed wonders nonetheless denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' looks like 'performed' in the surface, but it is the anagram signal; DI is British police shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement denying responsibility or knowledge is a repudiation of a claim.

clue.text: Can east European dance round it?

parts.note: may means can, be allowed to
a Pole comes from Poland, in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man from Eastern Europe is able to dance in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Villagers dance round the beribboned pole on May Day; the question mark flags the descriptive definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall ribboned pole of English spring festivals is the thing folk dancers circle.

clue.text: Trainee tucked into hot German bread

indicators.note: the trainee's letter is placed inside the word for hot

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: An apprentice eating warm loaf from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a fruited loaf eaten in Germany at Christmas.

clue.text: It's reasonable for an American soldier to enter pub

indicators.note: the soldier goes into the word for pub

parts.note: your local is your neighbourhood pub
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: Asks whether it makes sense for a US serviceman to go into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensible and sound in its thinking follows reason.

clue.text: Help someone perform a stylish pirouette

parts.note: to do is to perform
good can mean fine, well executed
a pirouette is a spinning turn

explanation.surface: A dancer asked to execute an elegant spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a kind deed for another person is an idiom for assisting them.

clue.text: Use one's fists to render Jack unconscious

parts.note: render and unconscious together mean knock out, to make senseless; render supplies the first half
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor or jack
out means unconscious

explanation.surface: Advice to punch a man named Jack senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for rendering someone unconscious is split in two by the sailor, who sits between its halves in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone about is to hit them repeatedly, as in a brawl.

clue.text: Manage to send policeman to Gravesend

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
read as grave's end, the last letter of grave

explanation.surface: Dispatching an officer to the Kent town of Gravesend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town in Kent, but split it as grave's end: E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to get by or handle a difficulty.

clue.text: Asking the question again while lying down?

definitions.meaning: putting a query a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Split as re-posing it means putting a query once more; as one word it means resting at ease.

clue.text: Liberal put in different word for "heaven"

parts.note: other means different

indicators.note: the Liberal letter is placed inside word

explanation.surface: A politician choosing another term for paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is a realm beyond this one, a spiritual afterlife.

clue.text: Soft-headed nobles — but they're gems

indicators.note: the soft letter goes at the head of the nobles

parts.note: p (piano) is the music abbreviation for soft
earls are noblemen

explanation.surface: Dim-witted aristocrats, yet treasured nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-headed' looks like foolish; it means the nobles are headed by P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls are precious things worn as jewels.

clue.text: Maybe a professor of horology is too punctual

definitions.meaning: the leading figure of clock-making, read as three separate words

explanation.definitionFit: Read as separate words it is a chief of clocks; as a phrase it means early.

clue.text: Tea set he designed shows he has exquisite taste

indicators.note: the letters of tea set he are designed afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A man of refined taste reveals himself through a china set he created.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to beauty and refined art.

clue.text: Stay a day in France in child's housing

indicators.note: the son contains the French day

parts.note: a son is a child
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A short visit of one day to France, lodging with a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary residence somewhere.

clue.text: Ask question of one of the choristers, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is said aloud and heard as a single word

parts.note: a chorister is a member in choir

explanation.surface: Questioning a singer in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the choristers' is someone in choir, which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enquire is to ask.

clue.text: Actors tread them; directors are on them

definitions.meaning: company directors sit on governing panels

explanation.definitionFit: Stage planks are trodden by performers, and company directors sit on governing panels.

clue.text: Tree found by river in Devon, initially

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Devon

explanation.surface: A tree spotted beside a West Country river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river on the Devon-Cornwall border in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree whose pods yield a sour pulp.

clue.text: Illness affecting youth in spring

indicators.note: the youth sits inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a spring month
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young person caught a bug in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is a disease or ailment.

clue.text: Such a dancer must be dynamic

explanation.definitionFit: A club entertainer performs as a go-go dancer, and the term also means energetic and lively.

clue.text: Criminal sentence for unyielding lefties?

parts.note: hard means unyielding
Labour is Britain's left-wing party

explanation.surface: A punishment for intransigent left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the main British left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour was a prison punishment of forced physical work.

clue.text: However viewed, it's a blunder

indicators.note: whichever way it is read, forwards or backwards, it is the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A mistake that looks the same from every side.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal for a silly mistake.

clue.text: Talk endlessly about the Spanish churchman

indicators.note: the talk goes around the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A gossip who won't stop talking about a Spanish clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' belongs to the definition of PRATE, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior cleric such as a bishop.

clue.text: Postpone proceedings to move elsewhere

definitions.meaning: suspend a meeting or court until later
go to another place, as in retiring to the lounge

explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is suspended until later, and a group may also relocate to another room.
